annotations.title: Look a Church Slavonic word up

description:
Look an Old Church Slavonic word up on Wiktionary and return its senses
plus full declension/conjugation tables — attested content (singular, dual
and plural), not invented. Any form of the word works; an inflected query
is resolved to its lemma automatically via previously cached paradigms and
the result notes the resolution. With search_language='eng' the query is
an English word instead: the result lists its per-sense Old Church
Slavonic equivalents (the translations block) plus their expanded entries.
Returns Markdown plus the same result as structuredContent matching the
declared outputSchema.

Results are cached server-side; first-time queries reach the live upstream
politely and calls are rate limited — on a rate-limit error, wait a few
seconds and retry. Content is from en.wiktionary.org (CC BY-SA 4.0 —
attribute and share alike if republished).

SearchLanguage.description:
The query language. ``chu`` looks an Old Church Slavonic word up directly
(any of its forms — an inflected query resolves via cached paradigms). ``eng``
searches in reverse: the English Wiktionary page for the query word lists
per-sense Old Church Slavonic translations, and each distinct lemma is then
looked up normally.
SearchLanguage.title: SearchLanguage

include_forms.description: When true (default), each match's full declension/conjugation table is returned INLINE — usable cases/tenses (singular, dual AND plural) in ONE call, no follow-up slavonic_get_inflections. Set false for a cheap screen of which entries exist. Bounded by a per-search cap — use max_forms to adjust per call. For eng queries this governs the expanded OCS entries; the per-sense translations list itself is always returned.
include_forms.title: Include Forms

max_forms.description: Optional override for how many inflection tables to expand this call (0–12). On an uncached query each table is one politely paced upstream fetch, so high values on cold queries are slow. Omit for the server default.
max_forms.title: Max Forms

query.description: The word to look up, in the language search_language names. Church Slavonic (default): a SINGLE Old Church Slavonic word in Cyrillic, any form — an inflected form ('бога') is resolved to its lemma ('богъ') automatically via cached paradigms, and the result says so; normalized OCS spelling works best, but titlos/accents and modern-Cyrillic respellings (ы for ꙑ) are folded. English (search_language='eng'): the English word whose Old Church Slavonic equivalents you want — multiword entries like 'apple tree' work.
query.title: Query

search_language.description: Language the query word is in: 'chu' (default) looks the Old Church Slavonic word up directly; 'eng' finds the OCS equivalents of an English word (per-sense, from Wiktionary's translation tables) and returns their full entries. Glosses are in English either way.

name: slavonic_search

Entry.description:
One Old Church Slavonic entry on the page: the headword (page title) with
one part-of-speech section's senses.
Entry.title: Entry

InflectionHandle.description:
A structured anchor for fetching a full paradigm: feed ``entry_id`` (the page
title) + ``word_class`` (the POS section) to ``slavonic_get_inflections`` — or ask
``search`` to include the table inline (``forms``).

entry_id.description: Wiktionary page title — the Cyrillic lemma itself.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

forms.description: The full paradigm, populated when a search is asked to include forms. None when not requested or beyond the cap.
forms.title: Forms

InflectionHandle.title: InflectionHandle

ParadigmNotFound.description:
No inflection table for this page/POS (no Old Church Slavonic section, no
table, or the page doesn't exist). ``found`` is False and there is no body.

Sense.description: One sense of an entry: the (HTML-stripped) Wiktionary definition line.
Sense.title: Sense

SlavonicNominalParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun/adjective/pronoun/etc.: case → {singular, dual, plural}.

Gender-split tables (adjectives, pronouns, participles) carry the gender — and,
for adjectives, the short/long variant — in the key: 'nominative masculine',
'long nominative feminine'. ``category`` discriminates this from the verbal and
not-found shapes — switch on it before reading the body.

cases.description: Case key (lower-case: 'nominative', 'genitive', …; gender and short/long variant prefixed when the table splits by them) → its singular/dual/plural forms, in table order.
cases.title: Cases

source.default: Wiktionary, the free dictionary (en.wiktionary.org), Old Church Slavonic entries. Wikimedia Foundation. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; attribution and share-alike required when republishing. (CC BY-SA 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) Adapted: reformatted and condensed from the original.
source.title: Source

SlavonicNominalParadigm.title: SlavonicNominalParadigm

SlavonicNumberForms.description:
A declension cell: the THREE number forms of one case — Old Church Slavonic
keeps a full dual. Forms are verbatim normalized OCS Cyrillic; alternates stay
comma-separated as Wiktionary renders them. A number the table doesn't give
(defective paradigms) is an empty string.
SlavonicNumberForms.title: SlavonicNumberForms

SlavonicVerbalParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb, grouped the way Wiktionary's table is: finite cells
keyed by tense/mood → person-and-number → form, plus the non-finite sections
(infinitive, supine, l-participle and the other participles).

finite.description: Tense/mood (lower-case, e.g. 'present', 'imperfect', 'aorist', 'imperative') → person and number ('first singular' … 'third dual' … 'third plural') → the form. Periphrastic rows (perfect, pluperfect, future) appear under the single key 'all'. Alternates are comma-separated; an em-dash cell (no such form) is omitted.
finite.title: Finite

nonfinite.description: Non-finite section ('infinitive', 'supine', 'l-participle') → label ('form' for the single-form sections; 'singular masculine' etc. for the participle) → the form.
nonfinite.title: Nonfinite

TranslationSense.description: One English sense (a translations table) and the OCS terms it offers.

sense.description: The sense gloss the source table carries.
sense.title: Sense

TranslationSense.title: TranslationSense

TranslationTerm.description:
One Old Church Slavonic word a translations table offers for an English
sense. ``word`` is the Wiktionary page title in Cyrillic (what an ``eng``
search re-searches and what ``slavonic_get_inflections`` needs); only the Cyrillic
script row is read — the parallel Glagolitic spelling is the same lemma on a
soft-redirect page, so surfacing it would only duplicate the term.

display.description: Rendered form when it differs from the title.
display.title: Display

qualifier.description: Usage qualifier as marked, e.g. 'poetic'; else empty.
qualifier.title: Qualifier

transliteration.description: Scientific romanization as Wiktionary prints it, e.g. 'voda'.
transliteration.title: Transliteration

word.description: Wiktionary page title — the Cyrillic lemma itself.
word.title: Word

TranslationTerm.title: TranslationTerm

outputSchema.description: The result of a dictionary search.

forms_truncated.description: How many handles did NOT get an inline table because the per-search cap was reached.
forms_truncated.title: Forms Truncated

found.description: False when nothing matched. For an eng query, True means Old Church Slavonic translations were found — entries may still be empty when none of them could be expanded (see translations).
found.title: Found

resolved_from.description: The original inflected query when resolved; else empty. chu queries only — always empty for eng results.
resolved_from.title: Resolved From

resolved_lemma.description: The lemma actually searched when resolved; else empty. chu queries only — always empty for eng results.
resolved_lemma.title: Resolved Lemma

search_method.description: How the match was found: 'direct' = the query itself matched; 'lemma_index' = an inflected form resolved via a previously cached paradigm; 'translations' = an English query resolved via Wiktionary translation tables.
search_method.title: Search Method

translations.description: Populated only for eng queries (always [] for chu): the OCS terms each English sense translates to, in sense order. Entries/handles below are the expanded dictionary entries of those terms.
translations.title: Translations
